text:
Maria Chen: Quick ping — PR #9135 is ready for merge but I'd like a perf sanity check first. Local canary shows p95 tail increase on 4k seq and a small host mem bump. Artifacts + traces: https://artifacts.internal/bench/9135. Can someone look and say if this is ok or a blocker?

Dan R.: thanks — can you paste the bench numbers here so it's easy to eyeball?

Maria Chen: sure, raw numbers from the canary run (baseline -> PR):
```
model: rwd-llm-7b
batch=8, seq=4096
p50: 82ms -> 84ms
p95: 198ms -> 222ms (+12%)
throughput: 1250 tok/s -> 1220 tok/s (-2.4%)
mem (host): 5.20GB -> 5.31GB (+110MB)
```

CI Bot: CI checks passed: unit tests ✅, integration smoke ✅. Canary perf job attached: https://ci.internal/jobs/9135/canary

Ashok Patel: hmm the mem bump is small, but p95 tail looks non-trivial. Do we have prefill vs sampling breakdown?

Maria Chen: traces are here: https://traces.internal/trace/9135-prefill and https://traces.internal/trace/9135-sample. Prefill shows an extra ~6ms around token 512 that correlates with additional kv fetchs — looks like a tiling/prefetch path got a little slower.

Sasha K.: could be related to the tiling/pack change in PR 9055 — did this PR touch shard packing or async prefetching? any evictions logged?

Maria Chen: I did adjust a tiling config and removed an experimental async prefetch path (I thought it was unused). I can re-run a microbench toggling that flag and post results.

Will L.: if this is tail-only and throughput/memory mostly fine, i'm okay with merging behind a canary rollout: 10% for 1h, then 50% if clean. objections?

Dan R.: +1 on canary rollout but please add a rollback guard and a perf alert (p95 > baseline * 1.10). Also note the canary should run the same traffic distribution as prod (long sequences).

Ashok Patel: i'll dig into the traces today and try to reproduce locally with prefilling reproducer. if i don't find a root we gate the mem/tail checks in canary.

Maria Chen: thanks all — starting 10% canary now and will post the canary run link + final go/no-go after 1h :thumbsup:
